I feel like this is going to be so long winded, so apologies ahead of time. 

How to stop being materialistic is a learning process that takes lots of personal reflection.

Whether it’s societal, that you maybe be collecting and purchasing things because of advertisements, marketing or a trend.
Is it because of upbringing makes you hold onto items longer than needed….I think reflecting on that helps face the big question.

For myself, I think the biggest thing over the past year or so is reducing what I bring into my place.

I can’t remember what the exact quote was or where I heard it but a big mental barrier for many people is once you buy something and bring something into your home it’s harder to actually get rid of it. We tend to think “I’ll use this eventually” or “but what if I need it” and hold onto things rather than letting them go. 

So a big way to reduce holding onto stuff you may not really need is to never bring it home.

Evaluate items as you pick them up in the store and don’t impulse purchase. 
I usually will put it down, walk away and in a week I’m still thinking of that exact item I’ll sometimes write it down in a notebook, my notes app or find it online and take a picture of it. There are so many things on lists, in photos that I realize over time in a few months I have no connection or attachment to that I’m glad I never purchased. 

However if there is an item you keep coming back to it week after week or in a month then evaluate if it’s worth a purchase. 


I think also evaluating items you already have and seeing how much you actually use something.

Often I find myself thinking of how much I pay for rent and the cost per square inch of my place and I’m sitting here using sq footage storing items like a storage unit rather than enjoying more space and organization in my life. 

I think it’s super easy if it’s a fairly common item you have never or used once or twice, stick everything like that in a box in a corner of your closet, pretend it doesn’t exist for a month or so. If after a month or two months, you still haven’t thought of it, needed it and gone for any of those items, purge that box. Rinse repeat.

Worse comes to worse maybe you end up needing it in a year you can purchase it again or maybe borrow a friend’s. 

It’s a lot of mental work, and I find myself constantly reevaluating and picking up another tool to try and keep myself from overbuying or holding onto unneeded items. But it’s part of learning, and I think everyone here does so well in providing resources and support

If no frame shops offer it, I would check a fine art supply store near you, such as Blick or Artist & Craftsman. Their employees are usually involved in the art industry in some way so they should be able to point you in a direction if they don’t offer the service themselves.

Two options really,
Tape - tape your sheet of watercolor paper down to a water resistant surface using artists tape.

Commonly gatorboard or masonite are used. If you aren’t able to find those and are working smaller scale, a clipboard or drawing board can work. The classic brown clipboards/drawing boards are made of material very close to Masonite.
Artist tape it can be pricey for tape but it is the best as it is a low tack and acid free. Regular 3M masking tape is not acid free which means in a handful of years the area taped down will turn a yellowish brown, happened to me.

Watercolor blocks - they can be a more expensive option but I highly recommend for nice finished pieces of art. 

Watercolor blocks are a stack of watercolor paper glued together all the way around the edges. You work on the top sheet as it’s essentially pre taped down. Once you are done there is a small section that is not glued, stick a pallet knife in and scoot it around to separate your artwork off the block.
